title: Fight Day — Tournament Operations
description: From doors open to results published. The flow that exercises the entire vertical tier: EventCard → BracketTree → Scorecard → FighterCard, with federation scoring authority and offline-first as correctness requirements (venue connectivity is unreliable).
trigger: An event moves to live. The promoter opens the event-day kit; judges get their assigned bouts; spectators get the live bracket.

mobile.rationale: Judge and promoter are at the venue, one-handed, in front of a crowd. Errors are public and unrecoverable. Scoring must never be lost — offline queue is a correctness requirement.

desktop.rationale: Federation oversight and promoter management: bracket overview, judge submission counts (0/3→3/3), provisional at 2/3, dispute queue.

tablet.rationale: Judges may use tablet at ringside; present mode lets the crowd see scores. Scorecard legibility at 360px is an open design problem.

steps.purpose: Set the event live and make it visible.
steps.rule: Live badge pulses red (identity, not risk). Score updates push to spectators. Offline: event opens with cached schedule, sync banner shows.

steps.purpose: Show the bracket before and during fights.
steps.rule: Seeded → live (with scores) → complete. Bye handling explicit. Offline: last-synced bracket, unconfirmed fights greyed, 'Scores will sync when reconnected' banner.

steps.purpose: 3 judges per bout from the federation-approved list.
steps.rule: License verified. Assignment works offline. Judge cannot see others' scores until submit.
Auto-tally, confirm, signed with judge ID (tamper-evident). Scores in mono always. Offline: 'Scores saved offline. Will sync when connected.'
Provisional result shown at 2/3 majority. A judge cannot lose a round — confirm is final for them.

steps.purpose: Result updates fighter records + federation rankings.
steps.rule: Winner highlight = primary-text, never red (loss is error-red). Records auto-update W/L/D. Dispute window 30 min.

offlineCorrectness: Scoring is the highest-stakes flow — a judge cannot lose a round. Every score stores locally before network. Sync conflicts: federation overrides always win.
